topic: Agent evals: start with 20-50 tasks from real failures, grade the output not the path, and use pass^k for consistency (Anthropic engineering)
text:
An AI agent that passes once can still fail the next run.

Anthropic's engineering team says to start evals early: 20-50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start.

Two habits from their guide:
1. Grade what the agent produced, not the path it took. Rigid step-order checks punish valid solutions.
2. Pick the metric to match the job. pass@k is the chance of at least one success in k tries. pass^k is the chance that all k succeed.

For a customer-facing agent, pass^k is the honest number, because users expect it to work every time.

What's the first failure you'd turn into an eval case for your agent?
